related_questions.question: Why is type 1 diabetes so hard?
related_questions.snippet: Over time, type 1 diabetes complications can affect major organs in the body. These organs include the heart, blood vessels, nerves, eyes and kidneys. Having a normal blood sugar level can lower the risk of many complications. Diabetes complications can lead to disabilities or even threaten your life.

related_questions.question: Can type 1 diabetes live normal life?
related_questions.snippet: People with Type 1 diabetes need synthetic insulin every day, multiple times a day in order to live and be healthy. They also need to try to keep their blood sugar within a healthy range. Since several factors affect your blood sugar level, Type 1 diabetes management is complex and highly individualized.

related_questions.question: Who is most likely to get type 1 diabetes?

text_blocks.snippet: Type 1 diabetes is most likely to be diagnosed in children, adolescents, and young adults. While it can occur at any age, it's less common for adults to be diagnosed with it later in life. A family history of type 1 diabetes, especially a parent or sibling, increases the risk.
Factors increasing the likelihood of developing type 1 diabetes:

list.title: Family history:
list.snippet: Having a parent, brother, or sister with type 1 diabetes significantly elevates the risk.

list.title: Age:
list.snippet: While it can develop at any age, the peak onset is in childhood, adolescence, and young adulthood.

list.title: Genetics:
list.snippet: Specific genes, particularly those in the HLA complex, are associated with a higher risk of developing type 1 diabetes.

list.title: Race/Ethnicity:
list.snippet: In the United States, type 1 diabetes is more common in white individuals compared to African American and Hispanic or Latino populations.

list.title: Environmental factors:
list.snippet: While the exact triggers are not fully understood, certain environmental factors like infections or exposure to viruses are thought to play a role in triggering the autoimmune response that leads to type 1 diabetes in genetically susceptible individuals.

list.title: Autoimmunity:
list.snippet: Type 1 diabetes is an autoimmune disease where the body's immune system mistakenly attacks and destroys the insulin-producing cells (beta cells) in the pancreas.

list.title: Low birth weight:
list.snippet: Some studies suggest a link between low birth weight and an increased risk of developing type 1 diabetes, according to WebMD.
